title: Infra GPU Fleet Capacity, Cloud Accounts & CI/CD Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook consolidates the operational guidance, Terraform/IaC conventions, CI/CD patterns, cloud account and networking considerations, and runbook procedures for Redwood's GPU fleet and capacity management. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for provisioning, scaling, and operating GPU-backed inference capacity across cloud accounts and private deployments.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: GPU pool provisioning, capacity forecasting, account and VPC networking patterns, Terraform module usage, CI/CD pipelines for infra changes, incident runbook for capacity and networking events.
- Goals: predictable capacity provisioning, safe and auditable IaC changes, fast recovery from capacity/network incidents, and clear ownership.

Ownership and contacts:
- Fleet owner: eng-infra@gitlab.redwood (primary: @ashapatel)
- Oncall escalation: #infra-oncall (Slack), PagerDuty service: infra-gpu-capacity
- Network owner: @marcus-nguyen
- Terraform/IaC lead: @diego-morales

Key SLAs and thresholds:
- Allocation SLO: 99.5% of scheduled capacity available for Dedicated pools during business hours UTC-8 to UTC+2.
- Allocation safety margin: maintain 10% free headroom on critical pools (production-dedicated) to absorb sudden load.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - Pool_utilization > 85% (warning)
  - Pool_utilization > 95% for 5m (critical - page oncall)
  - Failed_node_registration >= 3 in 10m (critical)

Capacity planning process (recurring cadence):
1. Weekly telemetry review: infra team reviews per-pool utilization, tail latencies, and reservation vs actual usage. Data source: fleet-metrics (Prometheus) dashboards.
2. Monthly forecast: combine product roadmap forecasts with 90-day rolling average of peak usage and planned customer Dedicated reservations.
3. Purchase/Cloud commit alignment: translate required GPU hours to cloud instance reservations and committed spend; review with finance before 30-day procurement window.

Sizing guidelines and formulas:
- Effective GPUs required = ceil((expected_peak_token_rate * avg_tokens_per_request) / (tokens_per_second_per_gpu * target_utilization))
- Example: expected_peak_token_rate=120k tokens/s, avg_tokens_per_request=50 => request/sec=2400 rps; tokens_per_second_per_gpu=2500 => base_gpus = ceil((120000)/(2500*0.8)) = 60 GPUs (apply rounding to instance pod sizes).

Terraform & IaC modules (conventions):
- Use central modules in git repo: infra-modules/gpu_pool, infra-modules/gke_node_pool, infra-modules/vpc_peering, infra-modules/iam_roles.
- Module contract (required variables):
  - name (string)
  - region (string)
  - gpu_type (string, e.g., nvidia-a100-80gb)
  - desired_gpu_count (number)
  - instance_profile (string)
  - network_ids (list)

Example GPU pool module usage (terraform):
```hcl
module "prod_gpu_pool_bert" {
  source            = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra-modules.git//gpu_pool?ref=v1.8.0"
  name              = "prod-gpu-pool-bert"
  region            = "us-west1"
  gpu_type          = "nvidia-a100-80gb"
  desired_gpu_count = 64
  instance_profile  = "redwood-prod-gpu"
  network_ids       = [module.vpc.network_id]
}
```

Module release policy:
- Modules are versioned with semver tags in the infra-modules monorepo.
- Changes must include: upgrade guide, migration plan, and a downstream impact matrix.
- Major version bump requires approvers from infra, security, and platform teams.

CI/CD patterns for infra changes:
- Pipelines: every PR to infra repos triggers: fmt/lint, unit tests (terratest for modules), plan (in isolated ephemeral workspaces), and apply (manual gated).
- Deploy flow: PR -> terraform plan posted to PR -> approvals by two infra reviewers -> staged apply to "staging" account -> smoke tests -> 1-hour observation window -> apply to "production" account.
- Protected branches: main/master protected; requires signed commits and passing pipeline.

Example GitHub Actions CI pipeline snippet (conceptual):
```yaml
name: terraform
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  fmt:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - run: terraform fmt -check
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: fmt
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - run: terraform init
      - run: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
      - run: terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json
      - run: ./scripts/post-plan-to-pr.sh plan.json
```

Networking and cloud accounts guide:
- Account layout: one production account per cloud-region grouping (e.g., prod-us-west, prod-eu-west). Shared tooling and staging accounts used for CI/CD testing.
- VPC design: central VPC per region with subnet segmentation: control-plane, compute-gpu, storage, management.
- Peering and egress: use private peering for control plane to GPU pools; NAT gateways in management subnet for patching and images.
- Firewall baselines: allow only required ports for node registration (SSH for bastion; gRPC/HTTPS for runtime); deny all otherwise.

Runbooks: common procedures
- P1: Pool full / allocation < SLO (Immediate)
  1. PagerDuty page: infra-gpu-capacity -> oncall starts.
  2. Check dashboard: pool utilization, queue lengths (fleet-metrics dashboard).
  3. Quick mitigation (ordered):
     a. Promote standby pools or burst capacity policy (runbook command: `redwoodctl capacity promote --pool standby-gpu-pool --target prod-gpu-pool-bert --count 8`).
     b. Reduce non-critical scheduled jobs: toggle maintenance flag (`/api/v1/maintenance?job_type=training`) or pause CI heavy workloads.
     c. If immediate capacity needed, scale up node groups via Terraform emergency workspace: tag emergency=true and run `terraform apply -var="desired_gpu_count=+16"` (only after approval from infra lead).
  4. Post-incident: perform RCA, update capacity forecasts, and file follow-up ticket with backlog priority.

- P2: Node registration failures / provisioning errors
  1. Inspect cloud provider instance state and kube kubelet logs on node (SSH via bastion).
  2. Run: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` and inspect `dmesg` for driver errors.
  3. Common fixes: driver reinstall (nvidia-driver-agent), restart kubelet, or reprovision instance.

Operational tooling & commands:
- redwoodctl (internal): capacity commands, pool queries, and emergency promotions.
- Observability: Grafana dashboards (gpu-pool-utilization, gpu-node-health), Prometheus alertmanager rules stored in repo: infra-monitoring/alerts/gpu-alerts.yaml.
- Metrics to monitor: gpu_utilization_pct, pod_queue_length, node_registration_latency, image_pull_failures.

Maintenance windows and upgrades:
- Upgrade plan: staggered node pool upgrade with 10% draining at a time; test on staging pool before production.
- Rolling upgrade command example: `terraform apply -target=module.prod_gpu_pool_bert.node_pool_upgrade` followed by health checks for 30m.

Post-incident and retrospectives:
- For any P1/P0 incident, create a postmortem within 72 hours and link to this page. Assign action owners and estimate work effort.

Appendix: quick reference snippets and links
- Terraform module repo: git@repo/infra-modules.git (see gpu_pool/README.md)
